title: AI in Staffing: Hype or Real?
summary: Is AI for real? Or just hype? This guide breaks down the difference between automation and AI, reveals dozens of specific use cases across every staffing function from recruiting to payroll, and honestly addresses what AI can't do yet (spoiler: it's not replacing your people skills anytime soon). Whether you're skeptical about the hype or ready to experiment, this post will help you identify the high-impact, low-risk opportunities that could give your staffing company a real competitive edge.
body_text: AI in Staffing: Hype or Real? Traditionally, the staffing industry is not an early adopter of new technology. Our data shows that less than 5% of staffing companies offer their workers a mobile app. At the same time, staffing is a business that has very defined processes that are typically handled by humans, making it a great candidate for automation that enables humans to offload mundane aspects of their job and do more high-quality work. This thesis is a core driver of the solutions we make at Zeal. Now, we’re in the early stages of an AI technology boom, and we’ve been thinking about how a new wave of AI automation can allow staffing companies to do more with less. Automation and AI: Two Powerful Tools We see automation and AI as two pieces of a bigger solution that help staffing companies gain efficiencies: Automation is for deterministic, rule-based tasks. Workflows that are structured, regulated, and precise where accuracy and consistency are non-negotiable. These are the moments where you need outcomes that are predictable and provably correct, such as gross-to-net calculations, tax withholdings, and benefit deductions. When you don’t want to risk an error, automation is your tool of choice. AI , on the other hand, is emerging as a powerful force for handling less structured, less risky tasks that require contextual understanding, or where a human check is part of the workflow. AI enables things that were either too expensive or impossible to scale before such as rapid decision-making, personalized communication, dynamic learning, and insight generation. When you want to communicate with candidates, remind customers to pay, analyze lots of data, and more, AI is proving to be a useful tool. We’ve been thinking about how staffing companies can benefit from AI. Some of these tools we’ve built, some others have built, and most have yet to be built. We are still in the early days of AI in staffing and we hope to see much more AI (and automation) being built by the broader staffing community. This isn’t an exhaustive list, but it’s a strong foundation for exploring what AI can do in staffing today, and where it’s headed. Where AI Sits in the Hype Cycle Today We’re in the midst of what Gartner calls the “Peak of Inflated Expectations” for AI. The headlines are everywhere, startups are racing to launch “AI-powered” features, and investors are pouring money into anything with “AI” in the pitch deck. For staffing leaders, this can feel both exciting and overwhelming. The reality is that many AI use cases are delivering real value right now, but others are still years away from operational reliability. And in the staffing world it’s likely that more use cases are farther off from delivering real value. History tells us that this inflated expectations phase is usually followed by the “Trough of Disillusionment,” when unrealistic promises give way to more measured adoption and sustainable models. What this means for staffing: Look for safe bets . Think about how to adopt AI-assisted workflows that limit the impact of negative outcomes. Having AI write an email to send to a candidate recruiting has a pretty minimal impact if that copy is bad or wrong. Avoid high-risk bets. Avoid using AI to handle end-to-end processes, or having AI handle tasks with potential legal implications. Using AI to calculate overtime could be a compliance violation and a large penalty if it uses the wrong formula. Strategic timing . Early adopters who choose proven use cases now can build a competitive advantage, but those chasing unproven tech risk wasting budget and trust. Seek out operational wins. The AI hype cycle wants you to believe that using AI will bring you more revenue. In staffing, that’s highly unlikely. Remember AI is another form of automation. Look for the use cases that can improve your operational efficiency. AI in Demand AI is poised to become a cornerstone of sales and demand generation in staffing. It can help teams prospect more effectively, communicate faster, and extract insights previously buried in manual workflows. Key applications: Client sourcing : Use AI to identify potential clients based on job listings, company trends, social media posts, and more. Client outreach : Generate personalized outreach emails and LinkedIn messages using AI messaging and timing. AI job creation : Turn a few keywords or a client’s business profile into full job descriptions. Job intake via email : Parse client emails with AI to create job listings automatically in your ATS. Pricing intel : Use AI to benchmark market rates, analyze pricing trends, and recommend competitive pricing to win contracts. Deal upkeep: Have AI listen to your calls and update your CRM with relevant information and insights. ‍ Demand alerts: Predict when existing clients are likely to have hiring needs soon based on seasonal trends or company news. ‍ Lead scoring: Score inbound leads based on their likelihood to convert using AI classification models. AI in Recruiting AI is already making a major impact on recruiting. Recruiting assistants can now handle repetitive tasks, evaluate candidates, and surface hidden gems in talent pools. Key applications: Candidate sourcing : AI agents can crawl public databases and social platforms to identify qualified candidates based on required skills. Candidate outreach : Automate personalized outreach via email, SMS, or chatbots. A/B testing built in to improve performance. Candidate screening : AI can review resumes and responses, conduct initial assessments, and even perform asynchronous interviews. Candidate matching : Use machine learning to match candidates to jobs based on qualifications, availability, and cultural fit. ‍ Engagement optimization: Use sentiment analysis to evaluate candidate engagement and optimize communication timing. ‍ Pipeline creation: Recommend training to underqualified candidates who could qualify for future openings. AI in Onboarding Onboarding is a bottleneck in most staffing workflows. AI can streamline it, ensure compliance, and make it more engaging for workers. Key applications: Smart onboarding flows : Dynamically adjust onboarding checklists based on worker type, location, and client needs. Agentic onboarding support : Let workers chat with an AI agent that answers onboarding questions and walks them through forms. Candidate training : Offer just-in-time microlearning modules generated by AI based on job requirements. ‍ Multi-language support: Auto-translate onboarding materials for multilingual workers. ‍ Document verification: Detect incomplete or inconsistent documents in real time and prompt for correction. AI in Scheduling Filling shifts at the last minute is one of the hardest parts of staffing. AI can help anticipate needs, automate communications, and optimize schedules. Key applications: Intelligent scheduling : AI can match availability, compliance constraints, and preferences to auto-fill shifts. Compatibility matching: Match shifts not only by availability, but by historical performance, client satisfaction scores, and personality fit. Shift fill communication : Use AI agents to contact available workers via SMS, push notification, or voice bot until a shift is filled. ‍ Attendance scoring: Predict which workers are most likely to show up or call out based on past behavior. ‍ Compliance controls: Automatically ensure that workers aren’t scheduled for shifts that violate labor laws. ‍ Forecasting: Forecast future demand to preemptively build availability pools. AI in Timekeeping AI can help make sure timekeeping is accurate, fair, and compliant with minimal effort from managers or workers. Key applications: Time validation : Detect anomalies in submitted hours such as clock-ins outside of scheduled times or missing breaks. Presence verification : Use GPS, geofencing, and facial recognition to verify physical presence at job sites. Create AI engagements that verifies people are with their phone. Use AI to analyze badge swipe data or Wi-Fi pings for passive presence validation. Fraud detection: Detect patterns like “buddy punching” by analyzing clock-in proximity, swipe data, and behavioral anomalies over time. Compliance alerts: Notify your staff if a worker misses a clock-out that could result in a labor law violation. AI in Payroll Payroll is one of the most critical areas to get right. While much of it should be fully automated, AI can offer new layers of intelligence and adaptability. Key applications: Automate time-to-pay workflows : Seamlessly connect timesheets, validations, and pay runs using AI-assisted rules. Pay compliance : Automatically flag pay rule violations or missing withholdings based on evolving jurisdictional laws. Automated garnishments : Detect, categorize, and apply garnishments from scanned mail, emails, or digital files. ‍ Cash flow management: Forecast cash flow based on upcoming payroll liabilities. ‍ Error avoidance: Predict payroll errors before they happen by identifying edge cases in the data. AI in Billing Billing is often a manual and error-prone process. AI can accelerate and improve accuracy throughout the lifecycle. Key applications: Invoice generation : Automatically create client invoices from timesheet and rate data. Payment reminders : Use AI to send intelligent reminders based on client behavior. Payment collection : Deploy chatbots or agents to follow up on unpaid invoices. Late fee invoice updates : Dynamically update invoices to reflect penalties. Revenue recognition : Classify and forecast revenue automatically with contextual understanding of contracts. ‍ Data entry: Use NLP to extract and input invoice terms and payment timelines from client contracts. AI in Support AI is transforming support, from how issues are triaged to how teams learn from them. Key applications: Support chatbot : Instantly answer common questions from clients, candidates, or workers. Ticket prioritization : Auto-categorize and prioritize tickets based on urgency and impact. Issue reminders : Nudge agents or clients to respond to open issues. Agent coaching : Use AI to analyze support transcripts and coach agents on tone, resolution quality, and missed opportunities. Compliance guardrails : Monitor chat or ticket logs for language that could indicate compliance risk. ‍ Contextual highlights: Summarize past interactions for agents so they can respond more quickly. ‍ Support QA: Detect burnout or overwork in support staff through interaction analysis. AI in Reporting Reporting isn’t just about data, it’s about turning data into action. AI can help everyone from recruiters to execs understand what’s going on, fast. Key applications: Automated P&L and dashboards : Generate live profitability reports by client, job, or location. Insights chatbot : Ask questions in plain English and get accurate, real-time answers. ‍ Intelligent alerts: Let AI monitor data and alert you when key metrics trend in the wrong direction. ‍ Scenario forecasting: Use predictive analytics to model future scenarios (e.g., what happens if client X stops hiring?). ‍ Industry benchmarking: Use aggregated, anonymized industry data to highlight how a company compares in fill rates, time-to-fill, and turnover. ‍ Action reports: Go beyond the data analysis and insights by getting recommendations for next steps and possible solutions. What AI Can’t Do for Staffing (Yet) AI can do a lot of impressive things, but it’s not ready to replace hard rules or human judgment in many parts of staffing. Let’s be clear about the limits and avoid disappointment. It can’t replace people skills. Staffing is built on relationships. AI can help you send messages faster or match resumes to jobs, but it can’t truly build trust, negotiate delicate situations, or understand a customer's problem the way an experienced human can. Gino Rooney, former CEO of BlueCrew, said on Episode 1 of the Great Work Podcast : “I don't believe you can have a completely autonomous staffing agency because I do think there is a really real component to having customer service as a competitive advantage.” It can make mistakes. While AI can be accurate, it’s not flawless. Unlike automation, which produces deterministic outputs given the same inputs, AI operates on probability and prediction. That means it can be right most of the time, but not all the time—and that distinction matters when accuracy is mission-critical. Sometimes it will misunderstand a job description, miss a great candidate, or give advice that just doesn’t fit your specific situation. Again, don’t use AI when the stakes are high. Use automation where precision is paramount; use AI where adaptability and speed are more valuable than perfect accuracy. It still needs supervision. AI works with the information it’s given. If the data is incomplete or outdated, it can make recommendations that miss important context. Avoid having AI do high value tasks without human review. Think of AI as a smart assistant, not a fully independent employee. You still need people to review its work, make final calls, and step in when something doesn’t look right. One guideline we have on the Zeal marketing team is “AI can be an input, but not the output.” It can’t handle every edge case. The staffing world is full of unusual situations—last-minute client changes, special payroll rules, or a candidate who needs extra onboarding help. AI is good at patterns, but humans are still better at handling the unexpected. How Staffing Leaders Should Engage with AI Today Jumping headfirst into every AI trend isn’t the goal—strategic adoption is. Every staffing company has a different maturity when it comes to their operations and readiness for AI. Using AI in the right places depends on your industry, clients, workers, and internal processes. Use the following steps as a guide to figure out what could work for your organization. Audit Current Workflows Look for repetitive, time-consuming tasks with clear rules and for judgment-based, unstructured tasks that still require manual work and consume your team's time. Pilot High-Impact Use Cases Start with AI applications that save significant operational hours. Set clear goals and metrics that combine the operational efficiency and the task completion such as tracking time saved alongside placements made, fill rate improvements, fraud rates, etc. Layer AI on Top of Automation Think of automation as your deterministic foundation. It’s the layer that guarantees accuracy and compliance. Then, layer AI on top to add flexibility, interpretation, and decision support. The combination gives you both reliability and adaptability: accurate results where risk is high, and intelligent support where experimentation is safe. Iterate, Then Scale Treat AI like an evolving partner, not a one-and-done project. Measure results, refine prompts and workflows, and then expand into adjacent areas once success is proven. Looking Ahead: Where AI Is Headed in Staffing Agentic AI Will Take on Bigger Chunks of Work We’re heading toward “agentic AI” where AI does more than answer a question, it actually takes a goal and carries it out across multiple steps. For staffing, that could mean giving an AI a request like “Fill this client’s weekend shifts” and having it source candidates, send outreach, confirm availability, update the schedule, and alert the client. This isn’t science fiction; early versions of these tools are already being used, and in the next few years, they could become a standard part of how staffing companies operate. AI and Automation Will Work Together Right now, automation handles the rule-based, repetitive stuff like running payroll or validating overtime and minimum wage compliance, while AI handles the “softer” side, like making recommendations or drafting messages. Over time, especially as agentic AI gets better, these two tools will combine to enable even greater operational efficiencies. That means your systems won’t just do the tasks; they’ll also decide which tasks to do, in what order, and how to adapt if something changes. Eventually this will happen across tools, giving you unified workflows that run almost entirely on their own, with humans stepping in only for oversight or exceptions. Building the Future of AI in Staffing Together We believe that, just like automation, there’s a place in staffing operations for AI—and that it's already beginning to show up in transformative ways. At Zeal, we’re not just building AI-powered tools; we’re building the infrastructure to support them. We’re just getting started. If you’re building AI for staffing, or dreaming of ideas we haven’t listed yet, let’s build this future together. ‍

Discussion of Results The discussion of results should be considered together with our unaudited financial information included with this review and the periodic reports we file with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including our Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. Recent Trends Total revenues grew 27% year-over-year to €120.0 million in the fourth quarter, primarily driven by Referral Revenue4 growth of 17%, or €15.9 million, compared to the same prior year period. We observed increased branded channel traffic in all trivago Core segments in response to our continuous strategic marketing campaigns, which continue to resonate well with our target audience. Additionally, numerous AI-related product improvements enhanced our hotel search experience and led to an all-time high booking conversion rate, which positively impacted our profitability. During the fourth quarter, we continued to further increase our Advertising Spend, which increased by 31% year-over-year, or €17.9 million, compared to the same period in 2024. Global ROAS decreased by 15.0 ppts to 147.9%, compared to the same prior year period due to our strong increases in brand marketing investments across all trivago Core segments. In addition, we tested additional branded marketing channels, which we anticipate to have further scaling potential going forward and are expected to mitigate risk through marketing channel diversification. The continued revenue growth observed this quarter confirms our brand strategy is working as effectively as planned. For the full year 2025, total revenues grew 19% year-over-year to €548.9 million, primarily driven by Referral Revenue of €532.9 million, which increased 17% compared to the full year 2024. Net income was €11.2 million and Adjusted EBITDA was €15.8 million, representing our ability to effectively scale our brand marketing strategy, while simultaneously growing our revenue baseline at profitable levels. Outlook Throughout 2026, we expect to improve profitability by continuing to scale brand marketing in our core markets at a more moderated pace than in 2025, benefiting from the compounding brand effects of our elevated investment levels in recent years. Additionally, we believe continued product improvements, an increasing number of logged-in members, and a seamless "Book & Go" user experience will further increase booking conversion and create retention. We expect that these initiatives, combined with strict cost discipline, will further drive our profitability. We anticipate delivering double-digit year-over-year total revenue growth as well as improved profitability during the first quarter of 2026. For the full year 2026, we continue to expect double-digit year-over-year total revenue growth and an Adjusted EBITDA of at least €20 million. Revenue, Advertising Spend, and Return of Advertising Spend Referral Revenue & Other Revenue We match our users’ searches with large numbers of hotel and other accommodation offers through our auction platform, which we call our marketplace. With our marketplace, we provide advertisers a competitive forum to access user traffic by facilitating a vast quantity of auctions on any particular day. Advertisers submit hotel room and other accommodation rates and participate in our marketplace primarily by making bids for each user click on an advertised rate for a hotel or other accommodation on a cost-per-click, or CPC, basis. From time to time, we may exclude from Adjusted EBITDA the impact of certain items that affect the period-to-period comparability of our operating performance. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure. A “non-GAAP financial measure” refers to a numerical measure of a company’s historical or future financial performance, financial position, or cash flows that excludes (or includes) amounts that are included in (or excluded from) the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP in such company’s financial statements. title: Arbe Appoints Ram Machness as Chief Executive Officer; Kobi Marenko Appointed President
body_text: With Arbe Advancing Into Its Next Strategic Phase, the Company Is Reinforcing Its Leadership Structure to Support Scaling, Deepen Customer Engagement, and Drive Long-Term Value Creation TEL AVIV, Israel , Feb. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Arbe Robotics Ltd. (NASDAQ: ARBE) (TASE: ARBE), a global leader in perception radar solutions, today announced that it is strengthening its leadership team as the Company advances into its next strategic phase. The Company has appointed Ram Machness, Arbe's Chief Business Officer, as Chief Executive Officer and appointed current CEO and co-founder Kobi Marenko as President. The official transition to the new roles will take place on April 1, 2026. Ram Machness brings more than 30 years of experience across embedded systems, semiconductors, and the automotive industry. At Arbe, Mr. Machness served as Chief Business Officer for the past eight years, since nearly the Company's inception, leading strategy, sales, customer support, and product functions. He spearheaded global OEM and Tier 1 engagements and led the Company's commercial and product strategy. Previously, Mr. Machness spent 12 years in senior business roles at Texas Instruments, where he led product lines and business strategy for wireless connectivity across automotive, mobile, and IoT markets. He began his career in core R&D, leading the development of deep embedded products. As CEO, Mr. Machness will lead Arbe's transition into a scaled production company, growing near-term revenue by expanding Arbe's presence in Level 4 robotaxi and robotruck markets, as well as autonomous commercial and off-road vehicle markets, and by continuing to advance automotive OEM and Tier 1 programs. He will also accelerate global business development, particularly in China, while strengthening the Company's long-term vision through deeper OEM collaborations and continued development of Arbe's next-generation radar solutions. Kobi Marenko, Arbe's current CEO, will continue with Arbe as President, working closely with Mr. Machness to support the successful execution of the Company's strategic plans and to ensure a seamless leadership transition. In his new role, Mr. Marenko will drive Arbe's long-term strategy, advance initiatives particularly in the defense market, develop key partnerships, explore strategic alternatives, and guide investments to help accelerate the Company's sustainable, long-term growth. Mr. Marenko will continue to serve as a director of the Company. "I want to express my sincere appreciation for the trust and confidence placed in me by the Board of Directors and Arbe's co-founders, Kobi Marenko and Noam Arkind," said Ram Machness. "I am grateful to Kobi for leading Arbe from its inception and building the strong foundation upon which Arbe is now able to transition into serial production and full commercialization. As we enter this next phase, I am excited about the opportunities ahead and fully committed to executing on our priorities and leading Arbe into the growth and success chapter." A bout Arbe Arbe (Nasdaq: ARBE), a global leader in ultra-high-resolution radar solutions, is driving a radar revolution. Its cutting-edge radar chipset delivers up to 100 times more detail than other radar systems on the market, empowering automakers and radar Tier 1s to develop safe driving systems that scale from ADAS to hands-free, eyes-off capabilities and up to full vehicle autonomy. Arbe's technology addresses the most critical use cases by delivering real-time, 4D imaging that enables the perception stack with information such as precise mapping of drivable free space in highway and urban environments across all weather and lighting conditions. With its transformative impact across passenger, commercial, and industrial vehicle segments, as well as other advanced safety applications, Arbe is redefining the role of radar in next-generation mobility. Headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, the Company also operates offices in the United States, Germany, and China. title: How Saie Turns Everyday Beauty Merch into Real Community Connection
summary: Discover how Saie uses everyday beauty merch to build real community, drive loyalty, and turn physical products into meaningful brand touchpoints.
body_text: Today’s most culturally relevant beauty brands are rewriting how to use beauty merch to promote products, create a memorable brand, and build a community built on high standards. Instead of treating promotional products as an afterthought, they’re using physical products as strategic tools for community building, creator engagement, and long-term brand loyalty. ‍ One brand quietly leading that shift? Saie. ‍ Saie, pronounced “Say,” was founded in November of 2019 by Laney Crowell and has quickly grown into one of the most recognizable clean-beauty brands among Gen Z and millennial consumers. Known for its skin-loving formulas, minimalist aesthetic, and community-first mindset, Saie has built far more than a product portfolio—it’s built a lifestyle brand where Saie beauty merch, accessories, and physical touch points play a meaningful role in shaping how people experience and connect with the brand. ‍ “Saie is a clean beauty brand on a mission to create positive change for people and the planet.” ‍ Photo courtesy of @SaieBeauty Instagram ‍ The Popularity of Saie Saie’s rise isn’t just about clean formulas (although this does play a big role) or trending products. The brand has positioned itself as a community-first beauty company—one that prioritizes transparency, accessibility, and participation. ‍ From creator partnerships to heavy user-generated content to feedback-driven product development, Saie makes customers feel like collaborators rather than consumers. And by prioritizing better-for-you ingredients and better-for-the-earth initiatives, the brand differentiates itself in a crowded beauty market, turning shared values into long-term loyalty. Merch, in this context, isn’t a standalone revenue stream. It’s a physical extension of that philosophy. ‍ Photo courtesy of Saie ‍ Pop Up Events Saie also uses Cafe Saie, a pop-up shop, to build brand awareness and engage with its community. The two-day event offers specialty coffee, like their exclusive Saie matcha lattes, as well as exclusive merch. In addition, there is a mobile vanity so attendees can touch up their makeup and get personalized recommendations from Saie Pro Artists. ‍ Photo courtesy of @SaieBeauty Instagram ‍ How Saie Redefines What Beauty Merch Can Be Rather than leaning into traditional merch, Saie focuses on functional lifestyle items, such as branded water bottles, high-quality cosmetic cases, and limited-time-only accessories, to drive awareness and create culture-first brand moments. These items feel useful and naturally fit into everyday routines, while still aligning with Saie’s clean, minimal aesthetic. In other words, the Saie merch strategy relies on brand-owned lifestyle touchpoints, instead of promotional objects. When a customer carries a Saie water bottle to Pilates or pulls a Saie cosmetic pouch out of their tote, that’s a brand impression. When a creator includes a Saie accessory in a GRWM video, that’s organic product placement. For Saie, merch isn’t about wearing the logo. It’s about living with the brand and embracing what it stands for. ‍ Photo courtesy of Saie ‍ While Saie merch is available on their website, viewers won’t find an endless supply of branded gear. Instead, Saie experiments with alternative merch models, like Saie Vintage , which reframes merchandise as a form of circular fashion rather than traditional promotion. By offering curated, secondhand apparel through limited drops, Saie reduces reliance on newly manufactured items while still giving its community something exclusive to engage with. It’s a rare example of a beauty brand using merch as a sustainability lever—proving that brand-building doesn’t have to come at the cost of overproduction. ‍ Photo courtesy of Saie Vintage from saiehello.com/pages/the-city-collection ‍ Saie’s Impact (Beyond Merch and Products) Saie’s climate initiative shows that sustainability isn’t a side project—it’s a built-in operating principle. Rather than treating environmental impact as a marketing claim, the brand approaches it as an evolving responsibility, investing in practices that address emissions, packaging choices, and long-term footprint reduction. The result is a brand that frames climate action as ongoing work, not a one-time badge—building credibility through commitment instead of perfection. ‍ ‍ Investing in Women Saie highlights the importance of investing in women as pivotal leaders in climate action. UN findings indicate that women often face the harshest effects of global climate change, yet they play a crucial role in promoting eco-friendly consumer habits and fostering broader societal shifts. In response, Saie has assembled an exclusively female board composed of specialists from different sectors, offering varied insights and established expertise to advance their sustainability targets. ‍ Image and content adapted from Saie's Climate Initiative page at saiehello.com/pages/the-saie-climate-initiative ‍ The Saie Way Docuseries With The Saie Way docuseries, the brand pulls back the curtain on what it actually takes to build a modern beauty company. Framed as an Earth-minded journey, the series brings Saie’s mission to life by showing—rather than telling—how the brand works toward positive change. From introducing a more sustainable approach to merch through Saie Vintage to supporting ocean-focused initiatives like Whale’s Paradise, viewers can see for themselves how Saie turns values into action. ‍ Image and content adapted from the Saie Way docuseries page at https://saiehello.com/pages/the-saie-way ‍ Recycling Program Saie makes it simple for customers to responsibly dispose of their used Saie products through a dedicated recycling program. They've partnered with Pact Collective to handle difficult-to-recycle beauty empties, turning what would otherwise end up in landfills into something more sustainable. The process involves thoroughly cleaning out the empty containers (ensuring no product residue remains), collecting at least five of them, filling out an online form to generate a prepaid shipping label, and then mailing the package or dropping it off if a local bin is available. This effort helps close the loop on hard-to-recycle packaging common in the beauty industry while keeping it simple to recycle Saie cosmetics. ‍ Thoughtful Packaging from the Start In addition to this take-back initiative, Saie emphasizes thoughtful packaging of Saie beauty products from the start—using biodegradable kraft shipping boxes that can be composted or recycled at home, 100% recycled FSC-certified paper for product cartons produced in carbon-neutral facilities, organic cotton balls as eco-friendly padding (instead of plastic alternatives), and water-activated cornstarch glue on their signature lilac kraft tape. ‍ Image and content adapted from Saie's official website, including the Recycling Program page at saiehello.com/pages/saie-recycling-program ‍ Every Body Campaign Saie takes its commitment to positive change beyond the environment and into social advocacy with The Every Body Campaign—a powerful, industry-leading initiative focused on reproductive justice. Powered by Saie and uniting over 60 brands from the beauty and wellness sectors, it's described as the largest beauty-industry-backed effort of its kind to support reproductive rights for all. ‍ The campaign partners directly with SisterSong: Women of Color Reproductive Justice Collective, a Black-women-led organization founded in 1997 that's the nation's largest multi-ethnic group advocating for reproductive justice, particularly for BIPOC communities most affected by restrictive laws. All proceeds from the campaign go toward SisterSong's work, which includes funding services for birthing people, parenting support, and abortion care—especially in impacted areas like Georgia, North Carolina, and Kentucky. Previous editions raised significant amounts (e.g., over $168,000 initially, with 2024 efforts aiming to exceed $300,000). ‍ Beyond fundraising, it encourages civic action: visitors are urged to register to vote, research ballots, make voting plans, and use their voices to protect bodily autonomy. Saie's founder and CEO, Laney Crowell (a mother of two daughters), emphasizes the brand's responsibility to leverage its platform for justice, stating it's about creating a more equitable future for women and birthing people everywhere. ‍ This aligns seamlessly with Saie's broader ethos of doing good for people and the planet, showing how the brand extends its values into human rights advocacy. ‍ Image and content adapted from Saie at everybodycampaign.com ‍ Building a Community: Saie Clean Beauty Crew Saie keeps customers coming back with their engaging rewards program, known as the Clean Beauty Crew on TYB. TYB stands for Try Your Best and is a community engagement and loyalty platform. By joining, fans can earn "Saie coins" through everyday interactions and purchases, which can then be redeemed for discounts on future orders like Saie makeup at saiehello.com. It's designed to reward not just shopping but also active participation in the clean beauty community. ‍ Key ways to earn coins include: Getting 5 coins for every dollar spent on Saie purchases through saiehello.com. Providing product feedback on Saie makeup and products, uploading user-generated content, leaving Saie beauty reviews, and completing other engagement activities or challenges on the TYB platform. ‍ Beyond the points system, members gain exclusive perks like early access to test new products before they launch, first dibs on purchasing limited releases, invitations to special events, and a chance to connect with like-minded clean beauty enthusiasts. ‍ To get started, simply sign up via their dedicated page—it's a fun, community-driven way to stack rewards while staying in the loop on Saie's latest drops and initiatives. ‍ Content adapted from Saie's official TYB rewards program page at saiehello.com/pages/tyb and related site sections. ‍ Photo courtesy of @SaieBeauty Instagram ‍ Saie's Lesson in Meaningful Merch From its clever pop-ups and sustainable packaging to community-driven rewards and bold advocacy and more, Saie shows how beauty brands can weave merch into something bigger—a real extension of their values that fosters loyalty and positive impact. By keeping things intentional, from limited-edition drops to eco-friendly accessories, they've turned everyday items into touch points that make fans feel seen and connected, all while championing people and the planet. ‍ The takeaway? In a world where consumers crave authenticity, thoughtful merch isn't just swag—it's a way to build lasting relationships. title: Cuenta en Europa desde Colombia: cómo Natalia construyó su vida global en España con Littio - Littio: Tu Cuenta en Dólares y Euros
summary: La app para recibir pagos del exterior, transferir sin fricción, pagar en cualquier país y recibir recompensas en USD* EUR* y COP*.
body_text: Mudarse a otro país nunca es tan fácil. Es un cambio de idioma, de rutinas, de referencias… y también de cómo manejas tu dinero en el día a día. Natalia Cárdenas, una colombiana que hoy vive en España , llegó a Madrid para cumplir un sueño: estudiar su máster, crecer profesionalmente y construir una nueva etapa de vida sin perder el vínculo con su familia en Colombia. Lo que no esperaba era que uno de los retos más grandes no fuera académico ni cultural, sino financiero: cómo moverse como local en Europa, pagar con tranquilidad y seguir conectada económicamente con su país de origen. Para Natalia, la respuesta no estaba en un banco tradicional, sino en su celular. Esta es la historia de cómo convirtió a Littio en su mejor aliado. Empezar de nuevo… también financieramente Como muchas personas que migran, Natalia llegó con preguntas muy concretas: cómo pagar el transporte, cómo cubrir gastos cotidianos, cómo recibir o enviar dinero sin fricciones y sin perder claridad en el proceso. Durante años había escuchado que manejar dinero entre países era complicado, costoso y lleno de trámites. Hasta que Littio apareció en su radar, casi por casualidad. Curiosamente, fue su mamá quien le habló de Littio. Natalia, con la prudencia natural de quien cuida su patrimonio, decidió investigar primero. “Yo no suelo meter dinero en algo que no entiendo. Si no me queda claro, no lo uso.” Ese enfoque marcó toda su experiencia. Te podría interesar: Las ventajas de recibir pagos en USDC frente a la banca tradicional en Colombia Una billetera en dólares y euros para una vida global Con el tiempo, Littio se convirtió para Natalia en su billetera digital que se ajusta a su vida entre países. Desde la app, puede mantener su balance en la moneda que necesita y usarlo con claridad, sin estar haciendo conversiones mentales todo el tiempo. Ella explica que lo que más valora es la simplicidad. En la app, sabe exactamente cuántos euros tiene disponibles para su vida en Madrid y cuántos dólares o pesos mantiene para otros fines. En sus palabras, la experiencia ha sido clara desde el inicio: “Para mí ha sido un sistema muy fácil, sin complicaciones.” Cuenta IBAN a su nombre: pagar y recibir como local en Europa Uno de los momentos clave en su proceso fue acceder a una Cuenta IBAN a su nombre desde Littio. En la práctica, esto significa tener un número de cuenta reconocido en Europa, que le permite recibir y realizar pagos como cualquier residente, sin procesos adicionales ni trámites complejos. Esto le permitió integrarse con mayor tranquilidad a la vida en España, recibir dinero y organizar pagos sin depender de procesos largos o confusos. Natalia cuenta que, al llegar a Madrid, todavía no tenía todo resuelto a nivel administrativo. Saber que podía manejar su dinero desde el primer día fue un alivio importante. “Cuando uno se muda a otro país tiene demasiadas cosas en la cabeza. Saber que el tema del dinero estaba resuelto me dio mucha tranquilidad.” Pagar en Europa y en Colombia, sin fricción Para Natalia, la tarjeta de débito internacional de Littio se volvió un respaldo constante. La usa para pagar transporte, mercado y gastos cotidianos en España, pero también cuando viaja dentro de Europa. Lo que más valora es que esa misma tarjeta funciona igual de bien en Colombia . Cuando regresa a visitar a su familia no tiene que cambiar de herramienta ni preocuparse por si va a funcionar o no en el día a día. Ella explica que, a diferencia de otros métodos, no siente cargos extra inesperados ni cambios confusos en el valor que ya tenía cargado. Un puente financiero entre países y generaciones La experiencia de Natalia no es solo personal. También es familiar. Su mamá, desde Colombia, ya usa Littio de forma autónoma. Incluso personas de generaciones mayores en su entorno han empezado a interesarse al ver lo sencillo que puede ser mover dinero entre países o poner a crecer su capital en monedas fuertes. Natalia cuenta que, al ver que a ella le funcionaba, su familia empezó a confiar y a usar la plataforma con más tranquilidad. Además mira: Cajeros automáticos en Europa. Cómo evitar tipos de cambio injustos y comisiones ocultas Una cuenta global en dólares y euros, pensada para personas reales Hoy, Natalia resume su experiencia con una idea simple: tener una cuenta global en dólares y euros le permitió enfocarse en su vida, no en resolver problemas financieros. Vivir con mayor tranquilidad en Europa. Seguir conectada con Colombia. Usar su dinero con claridad, aquí y allá. Mira acá su testimonio completo: Si estás pensando en estudiar, viajar o vivir en el exterior, o simplemente quieres una forma más clara de usar dólares y euros desde Colombia, la experiencia de Natalia demuestra que es posible hacerlo sin complicaciones innecesarias.
